name: useRef
desc: Returns a stable object with one mutable field, current. Writing current does not re-render, so it fits DOM nodes and values that must survive renders.
body:
The same object comes back on every render. React fills `current` with the DOM node after the commit and clears it to `null` when the node leaves the page.

Do not read `ref.current` during render. Use an effect, a callback ref, or an event handler.

name: ref on a DOM element
desc: Attaches a host element to a ref. React sets current after commit and resets it to null on unmount.

name: mutable instance value
desc: Keeps a value for the life of the component without causing renders. Use it for flags, request ids, and animation handles.

name: ref write does not render
desc: A ref assignment is a plain property write. React does not track it, so the screen only updates when something else renders.
body: If the number must change on screen at the moment of the click, it belongs in state. A ref is for values the user does not see, or for values that another render will display later.

name: initial value
desc: The argument is evaluated on every render but only the first result is kept. A function argument is stored, not called.

name: timer id
desc: Stores the id from setInterval or setTimeout across renders so the same timer can be cleared. Reset it to null after clearing.
body: In StrictMode the effect mounts, unmounts, and mounts again in development. Without this cleanup you would see two intervals and a clock that runs twice as fast. The cleanup is required in production too, where route changes unmount the component for real.

name: previous value
desc: Keeps the value from the previous render in a ref. The effect updates the ref after the render that used the new value.
body: On the first render the hook returns `undefined`, because no earlier value exists. Do not update the ref in the component body to get the value one render sooner: a render can run twice or be discarded, and the ref would then hold a value the user never saw.

name: focus after render
desc: Moves keyboard focus to a field after React inserts it. Guard against null because the node may already be gone.

name: scroll to an element
desc: Scrolls a node into view after it is committed. Use a marker ref at the end of a list for a chat style auto scroll.
body:
For a scroll container, `container.scrollTop = container.scrollHeight` is the alternative when you also need to read the old position and decide whether the user was at the bottom.

Use `useLayoutEffect` instead of `useEffect` when the jump must happen before the browser paints.

name: video control
desc: Controls a media element through its DOM methods. play returns a promise, so handle a rejected autoplay attempt.
body:
Read `currentTime` and `duration` from the element in a `timeupdate` handler when you need a progress bar. Do not drive playback from React state on every frame.

`muted` is what makes autoplay possible in most browsers. `requestFullscreen()` must be called from a user gesture.

name: callback ref
desc: A function ref receives the node on attach and null on detach. Runs at commit time, so layout reads are safe there.
body:
An inline arrow is a new function on every render, so React calls the old ref with `null` and the new one with the node. That is fine for a measurement and wrong for a subscription.

On React 19 a callback ref may return a cleanup function. An assignment expression such as `ref={(node) => (map.current[id] = node)}` returns the node, which React treats as a cleanup. Use braces to return undefined.

name: ref cleanup
desc: Cleans up timers, frames, listeners, and observers created around a ref. React clears DOM refs itself, but not the work you started.
body:
The cleanup must be safe to run twice, because StrictMode runs it during the extra mount cycle and the browser runs it on real unmount.

Clear the id and set the ref back to `null` or `0`. Leaving a stale id behind makes a second cleanup clear a handle that may already belong to another effect.

name: useImperativeHandle
desc: Exposes a small custom API from a child instead of the raw DOM node. Use it when a parent must call an action, not read the internals.
body:
The array works like the dependencies of `useMemo`. If a method reads a prop, list that prop so the parent receives an updated handle.

Keep the API small. A handle with many getters means the parent should receive props or lifted state instead.

name: ref forwarding
desc: Passes a parent ref through a function component to a DOM node. React 19 also accepts ref as a normal prop.

name: StrictMode and refs
desc: In development StrictMode renders twice and remounts effects. Refs created on the discarded render are thrown away, and missing cleanups show up as doubled work.
body:
Do not remove StrictMode to hide a doubled interval or a double fetch. The missing cleanup is the bug, and it will surface in production when a route change remounts the component.

An initializer with a side effect also runs twice. Keep ref initializers pure, or use the lazy `current === null` pattern for expensive pure values.

name: useRef mistakes
syntax: // read refs in effects, handlers, or callback refs
desc: The recurring errors: reading during render, using a ref for displayed data, missing null checks, and leaving stale timer ids.
body:
Checklist against the usual failures:

- Use state when the value is drawn. A ref that the JSX reads looks one render stale.
- Guard `ref.current` at the point of use, especially after `await`.
- Reset timer and frame ids after clearing.
- Never call `useRef` inside a condition or a loop.
- Do not put side effects in the initializer; StrictMode runs it twice.
- Do not pass a ref to a function component that neither forwards nor accepts it.
- Do not return an assignment from a callback ref on React 19.
